question: As per the Constitution of India, every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of ______ hours of such arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate.
solution:
The correct answer is __**24 hours**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **24 hours** is the maximum period within which a person who is arrested and detained in custody must be produced before the nearest magistrate, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate.
 
• This provision is enshrined in Article 22(2) of the Constitution of India.
 
• It ensures that the arrested person is not detained arbitrarily and has the opportunity to be heard before a judicial authority.
 
• This safeguard is part of the fundamental rights provided to individuals under the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** provides a comprehensive legal framework for the protection of individual rights and liberties.
 
• Article 22 provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• It mandates that no person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed of the grounds of such arrest.
 
• It also provides the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of their choice.
 
• Furthermore, it ensures that the person is presented before a magistrate within 24 hours, thus preventing unlawful detention.
